title: Bump Go to 1.27.2
body:
This PR updates Go to the latest stable release.

* **go directive:** `1.27.0`
* **toolchain:** `go1.27.2`
* **golangci-lint:** `v2.14.0`
* **govulncheck:** `v1.8.0`

title: Leave validation checks to CI in bump-go script
body:
<!--
Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the
change, rationale, and evidence within the context of the repository and pull request. Do not
narrate how the pull request was produced or refer to private conversations, prior agent work,
or other behind-the-scenes context. Omit those details unless they materially affect review;
if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

The scheduled Bump Go workflow runs `.github/workflows/scripts/bump-go.sh --apply`, which bumps the Go toolchain, then runs `go fix`, `go test ./...`, `golangci-lint`, and `govulncheck`, and exits before pushing or opening a PR if any of them fail.

[Run 37879027695](https://github.com/cli/cli/actions/runs/37879027695), bumping to go1.27.2, failed only because `govulncheck` reported reachable advisories in `golang.org/x/net` v0.58.0 (GO-2026-6617, GO-2026-6612, GO-2026-6611, GO-2026-6610, GO-2026-6603, all fixed in v0.60.0). A Go toolchain bump cannot fix a dependency advisory. A standalone `x/net` bump PR also fails Lint's `govulncheck` job, because the current go1.27.1 toolchain has stdlib advisories that are only fixed in go1.27.2. Each fix on its own fails `govulncheck`, so the bump automation is stuck.

This PR makes the bump script only generate changes. It still runs `go mod tidy` and `go fix ./...` and updates the golangci-lint and govulncheck pins, but it no longer runs tests, golangci-lint, or govulncheck. PR CI already runs all three on the bump PR: `go.yml` runs `go test -race -tags=integration ./...` on three OSes, and `lint.yml` (triggered by `go.mod` and `.github/golangci-lint-version` changes) runs golangci-lint at the pinned version, `go mod tidy -diff`, `go fix -diff`, and `govulncheck`. A failure then shows on the bump PR, where maintainers can push fixes, instead of stopping the PR from opening.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I ran `bash -n .github/workflows/scripts/bump-go.sh` and saw no syntax errors. I ran `shellcheck` on the script and saw only two findings on lines 36 and 52 (SC2015, SC2034), both of which predate this change.

Given I was on this branch with a clean tree and `go.mod` at `toolchain go1.27.1`
When I ran `./.github/workflows/scripts/bump-go.sh go.mod` (dry-run, no `--apply`)
Then I saw it select go1.27.2, run `go mod tidy`, set the golangci-lint pin to v2.14.0, keep the existing govulncheck pin (`Go language version unchanged; keeping the existing govulncheck pin`), run `go fix`, and go straight to the dry-run diff with no test, golangci-lint, or govulncheck step. The diff bumped `toolchain` to go1.27.2 and `.github/golangci-lint-version` to v2.14.0, and the script exited 0. Afterwards I was back on my branch with a clean tree and the temporary `bump-go-1.27.2` branch had been removed.

I did not run the script with `--apply`.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- `go mod tidy` and `go fix ./...` stay in the script because they produce the changes; CI only checks them with `-diff`.
- All pin logic stays. `golangci-lint version --short` is still needed to write `.github/golangci-lint-version`, so the workflow's golangci-lint install step is unchanged. The govulncheck pin is still validated, refreshed when the `go` directive changes, and listed in the PR body, because CI's `govulncheck` reads it and its embedded `x/tools` must understand the new Go language version's syntax.
- The tradeoff is that a bump PR can open with failing checks. That is intended: the failure is visible on the PR, where a fix can be added, rather than silently blocking the bump.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

The whole change is in `.github/workflows/scripts/bump-go.sh`. `.github/workflows/go.yml` and `.github/workflows/lint.yml` contain the PR checks that now gate the bump. Earlier automated bump PRs #14442 and #14423 show those checks running on bump PRs.

body:

Thank you for contributing to GitHub CLI!

If you are proposing a fix for a security issue, STOP and follow .github/SECURITY.md instead.

Keep the entire pull request self-contained, reviewer-facing, and diegetic: describe the

if they do, state the relevant fact and its significance directly.
-->

<!-- List related issues here. Use `fixes` or `closes` keywords to associate an issue number. -->

### Description

<!--
What's the problem? How are we addressing it?

Write for a reviewer who has not worked in this part of the codebase. Give them the
background they need before the problem makes sense, and avoid jargon.
-->

`golang.org/x/net` v0.58.0 (an indirect dependency) is affected by five published HTTP/2 advisories that govulncheck reports as reachable from `gh` code, for example via `api.telemetryDisablerTransport.RoundTrip` → `http2.Transport.RoundTrip`:

- [GO-2026-6617](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6617)
- [GO-2026-6612](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6612)
- [GO-2026-6611](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6611)
- [GO-2026-6610](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6610)
- [GO-2026-6603](https://pkg.go.dev/vuln/GO-2026-6603)

All are fixed in v0.60.0. Because of these findings, the scheduled [Bump Go workflow](https://github.com/cli/cli/actions/runs/37879027695) fails its govulncheck step and can't open its go1.27.2 toolchain PR. This PR bumps `golang.org/x/net` to v0.60.0. No other module versions change.

### How did you test this change?

<!--
Report only actions you actually performed and results you actually observed, using factual
first-person language (for example, "I ran..." and "I saw..."). Do not present planned,
hypothetical, inferred, or merely expected scenarios as testing.

Automated test results do not belong here. Passing unit tests, `go test ./...` output, and
coverage numbers tell a reviewer nothing they cannot see from CI, so do not paste them.

If you did not exercise the changed behavior, write `Not tested` and explain why.

Use one or more of these, whichever communicates best:

1. Screenshots or GIFs of the real command running. Preferred whenever the change is visible
   in terminal output. If output changed, show it before and after.
2. Given/When/Then scenarios, but only when you actually executed the steps. For example:
   Given I was in a repo with no open pull requests
   When I ran `gh pr list`
   Then I saw "no open pull requests in cli/cli"
3. A natural language walkthrough of what you did by hand, the states you covered, and what
   you saw, including error and edge cases.

If you leave this empty, your pull request will very likely be closed.
-->

I ran the pinned govulncheck (v1.8.0) locally with go1.27.1, before and after this change:

- **Before (trunk):** findings included the five advisories above, reported in `golang.org/x/net@v0.58.0`.
- **After:** govulncheck reported no findings in `golang.org/x/net`. The only remaining findings were 12 Go standard-library advisories in `go1.27.1`, all fixed in `go1.27.2`.

I did not manually exercise `gh` HTTP behavior.

### Key points

<!--
Tradeoffs you accepted, alternatives you rejected, and anything a reviewer would otherwise have to guess at.
-->

- **The govulncheck job in Lint is expected to fail on this PR.** Lint sets up Go from the toolchain pinned in `go.mod` (go1.27.1), and that toolchain still has the standard-library advisories. Those are fixed by the separate go1.27.2 toolchain bump, not by this PR.
- Once this merges, the scheduled Bump Go workflow should pass govulncheck and open its toolchain PR. That makes trunk's govulncheck green again.
- The alternative was a single PR bumping both the toolchain and x/net. I kept them separate so the existing Bump Go automation still produces the toolchain change.

### Notes for reviewers

<!--
Where should review start, and what should be read next? Call out anything you are unsure about.

Link related issues or prior discussion, with one sentence on why each matters.
-->

The diff is only `go.mod`/`go.sum`. The [failed Bump Go run](https://github.com/cli/cli/actions/runs/37879027695) shows the x/net findings that this PR resolves.
